briefs.headline: Jazz beat Spurs 119-109 in Utah as San Antonio rests its starters
briefs.summary: Victor Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox, Devin Vassell, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper all sat on coach's decision Monday in Salt Lake City. Harrison Barnes scored 19 and Tarris Reed Jr. had 17 rebounds. Phoenix visits Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Judkins and Schwesinger day-to-day with ankle injuries, Monken says
briefs.summary: Running back Quinshon Judkins and linebacker Carson Schwesinger left Sunday's loss at the Jets in walking boots; Todd Monken said Monday both are day-to-day. KC Concepcion is in concussion protocol before Sunday's 1 p.m. ET Ravens game.

briefs.headline: Bengals lean on Perine and inside zone to revive the run game
briefs.summary: Samaje Perine had a season-high 14 carries for 68 yards in Sunday's 31-24 win at Miami after 13 carries in the previous four games; ESPN Research counted 36.7% of called runs as inside zone. Cincinnati (3-2) is on its bye this week.

briefs.headline: Beilein says he 'cried like a baby' at WVU Hall of Fame induction
briefs.summary: John Beilein, who left Morgantown for Michigan in 2007, was inducted into the WVU Sports Hall of Fame Saturday, WV MetroNews reported Monday. 'I hated the way it ended in 2007,' he said. 'I love the way it is ending 19 years later.'

briefs.headline: Contreras homers, singles in go-ahead run as Brewers beat Dodgers 7-4
briefs.summary: William Contreras tied it with a 436-foot homer in the fifth and singled home David Hamilton in the sixth Monday in Milwaukee after a Freddie Freeman error; four relievers retired the last 15 Dodgers. Game 3 is Wednesday in Los Angeles.

briefs.headline: Lowe's two-run single in the eighth lifts Guardians past Rays 7-3
briefs.summary: Chase DeLauter and Patrick Bailey homered off Drew Rasmussen and Nathaniel Lowe broke a 2-2 tie Monday in St. Petersburg; Cleveland has won four straight in the postseason. Game 2 is Tuesday night, Parker Messick against Freddy Peralta.

briefs.headline: Dodgers to keep playing Ohtani unless he says he is hurt, ESPN reports
briefs.summary: Shohei Ohtani went 0 for 4 with two strikeouts Monday and has three hits in 20 postseason at-bats; Dave Roberts said he will talk with him at Tuesday's workout about the left knee and right biceps injuries that put him on the injured list.

briefs.headline: Rousseau's block, Bass's 45-yarder give Bills a 37-34 overtime win in LA
briefs.summary: Josh Allen passed for 210 yards and ran for 121 Monday night; Kyren Williams tied it with 4 seconds left, James Cook fumbled in overtime, then Greg Rousseau blocked Harrison Mevis and Tyler Bass kicked it with 1:55 left. Buffalo is 4-1.

briefs.headline: Senators beat Devils 4-1 for a fifth win in six since trading Tkachuk
briefs.summary: Tim Stutzle had a goal and an assist and Linus Ullmark stopped 29 of 30 Monday in Newark; Ottawa is 5-1-0 without Jake Sanderson, Artem Zub or William Eklund and lost Nikolas Matinpalo to a first-period boarding by Anthony Mantha.

briefs.headline: Wild beat Golden Knights 4-2; Sturm hospitalized after puck to the head
briefs.summary: Max Shabanov, Matt Boldy and Danila Yurov scored in the first period Monday in St. Paul, and Minnesota's penalty kill is 21 for 22, best in the NHL; Nico Sturm was taken for evaluation after Jared Spurgeon's slap shot hit his helmet.

briefs.headline: Coventry routs Newcastle 4-1, first home top-flight win in 25 years
briefs.summary: Jack Rudoni's sixth-minute penalty, Sidiki Cherif, Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni scored Monday for Frank Lampard's side, whose last Premier League home win came in April 2001; Sven Botman replied. Coventry is out of the relegation zone.

briefs.headline: Arteta defends post-match training after Hincapie, Zubimendi injuries
briefs.summary: Both hurt ankles in a session at the Emirates after Saturday's win over Leeds and had scans Monday; Arteta said Hincapie's "looks a little bit more serious" and both miss Tuesday's Champions League match with Lille.

briefs.headline: UCLA has 'serious concern' over Iamaleava's knee; no discipline for punch
briefs.summary: Bob Chesney said Monday doctors will set a timeline for the quarterback hurt in Saturday's win at Oregon, on a play where Bear Alexander twisted his helmet and struck him; Dan Lanning said the Ducks tackle will not be disciplined.

briefs.headline: Zverev clinches year-end No. 1 after Bergs upsets Alcaraz in Shanghai
briefs.summary: Zizou Bergs, ranked 39th, beat Carlos Alcaraz in straight sets Monday in the round of 32; with Jannik Sinner out for the season, Alexander Zverev, 29, the French and U.S. Open champion, becomes the oldest first-time year-end No. 1.

briefs.headline: Onosato targets a first Kyushu title as the jungyo reaches Kahoku
briefs.summary: The yokozuna (grand champion) did shiko (leg stomps) and suriashi (sliding steps) Tuesday at the jungyo (regional tour) stop in Kahoku, Ishikawa, and said he will soon resume practice bouts; he has never won the Kyushu basho (tournament).

briefs.headline: Tochinoshin backs Aonishiki to become the first European yokozuna
briefs.summary: The Georgian former ozeki (champion, second-highest rank), said Monday in Tokyo the Ukrainian "has that much strength," but warned him against competing hurt after his July yusho (championship) on a bad left ankle and toe.

The river read 1,340 cfs and 4.24 feet at 5:15 a.m. Monday, the true 24-hour mark and Monday's edition reading, so at 797 cfs and 3.47 feet it is down 543 cfs and 0.77 feet on the day; the fetcher's rising flags come from comparing against 48.8 cfs and 1.29 feet, the first point of its two-day window, the 6 a.m. Sunday base-flow reading, not 24 hours ago, and this morning that puts the direction backwards. The trace tells the whole weekend: 48.8 cfs at 6 a.m. Sunday, 57.5 at 11, 128 at 2 p.m., 1,760 at 5, a peak of 2,430 cfs and 5.51 feet at 7 p.m. Sunday, 1,450 at 2 a.m. Monday, 1,340 at 5 a.m. Monday, then a second push Monday morning, 1,390 at 6, 1,490 at 7, 1,530 at 8 and a secondary crest of 1,550 cfs and 4.51 feet at 9 a.m., before the recession proper: 1,440 at noon, 1,350 at 2 p.m., 1,270 at 4, 1,220 at 5, 1,150 at 7, 1,090 at 8, 1,010 at 10, 976 at 11, 943 at midnight, 910 at 1 a.m., 878 at 2, 852 at 3, 809 at 4, 797 cfs and 3.47 feet at 5 and 5:15 a.m. That is a third of Sunday's peak and still 16 times Sunday morning's base flow, falling 30 to 40 cfs an hour overnight and 12 in the last hour. The same rain is still in the Gauley: the Craigsville gauge above Summersville Lake (03189100) crested later, 4,250 cfs and 13.70 feet from 3:45 to 5 p.m. Monday, and read 2,990 cfs and 13.13 feet at 5:30 a.m.; the Gauley above Belva (03192000) peaked at 5,000 cfs at 1 a.m. Monday and read 3,980 cfs and 4.83 feet at 5 a.m.; and 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only, held 11.01 to 11.07 feet for two days and then dropped between 2:45 and 4:30 a.m. to 9.44 feet, which on the trace is the dam cutting its release in the last three hours, a reading of USGS traces and not a Corps statement. NWS's active product list for West Virginia was empty at 5:50 a.m., no flood watch, warning or advisory on the Gauley, Elk or Williams. At 797 cfs the river is still a brown push over the pocket water, the plunge pools and the undercuts, and there is no fly or leader to print for it; the fetcher's bank verdict stands. Sept. 22-23's high water took 19 days to recede to base flow, and the trace will say when this one is fishing.
waters.note: KNOWN FETCHER BUG, direction wrong this morning: the fetcher's 48.8 cfs and 1.29 feet comparison point is the first point of its two-day window, the 6 a.m. Sunday base-flow reading, not 24 hours ago, so it flags the river rising; the trace's true 24-hour mark is 1,340 cfs and 4.24 feet at 5:15 a.m. Monday, Monday's edition reading, and against it the river is down 543 cfs and 0.77 feet, falling on the day. The fetcher's numbers and flags are printed as the fetcher's and the correction is here. The river peaked at 2,430 cfs and 5.51 feet at 7 p.m. Sunday, had a secondary crest of 1,550 cfs and 4.51 feet at 9 a.m. Monday, and has fallen every hour since to 797 cfs at 5:15 a.m. No NWS flood product for West Virginia at 5:50 a.m. The Summersville release is read off USGS 03189600's stage trace (discharge series empty again; stage dropped 11.02 to 9.44 feet between 2:45 and 4:30 a.m.) and 03192000's discharge trace, not from the Corps. WVDNR's trout stocking page was not opened today; no stocking line is printed.

waters.working: Down on the day, up in the last three hours. The trace, pulled at 5:50 a.m., runs 26.03 at 5 a.m. Monday, the true 24-hour mark and Monday's edition reading, 26.10 at 11 a.m., 26.14 at noon, 26.22 at 2 p.m. and the window's high of 26.23 at 2:15 p.m., then a steady fall, 26.03 at 5 p.m., 25.79 at 7, 25.57 at 9, 25.40 at 11, 25.36 at midnight and 1 a.m., 25.31 at 2 a.m., the overnight low, and back up to 25.44 at 3, 25.54 at 4 and 25.56 at 5 a.m. That is down 0.47 on the day, so the fetcher's rising flag is wrong on the day, and up 0.25 since 2 a.m., so it is right at the hour. Its 25.16 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 6 a.m. Sunday reading (this morning's pull opens at 25.16), not 24 hours ago, and against it the pool looks up 0.40. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. What is still coming is the Gauley: on the USGS traces the Craigsville gauge above Summersville Lake crested at 4,250 cfs at 3:45 to 5 p.m. Monday and read 2,990 at 5:30 a.m., the Gauley above Belva read 3,980 cfs at 5 a.m. off a 5,000 peak early Monday, and 03189600 below Summersville Dam dropped from 11.02 to 9.44 feet of stage between 2:45 and 4:30 a.m., the dam cutting back on the trace; readings of USGS traces, not Corps statements, the Corps' Huntington District site not opened, so no lake elevation and no Corps release figure is printed. With the Kanawha's tributaries still well above base and the pool bumping back up overnight, the pool holds its color through the day. At 25.6 on a pool that crested Monday afternoon and is settling, the river fishes the edges of structure as the current eases: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked through the eddy behind each wing dam and along the downstream face of the riprap where the current breaks, a half-ounce blade bait on the inside of the creek mouths as they drain the last of Sunday's rain into the main river, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the slack of the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark, a 5 percent moon leaving the water nearly as dark as it gets. The lock wall at Byrd is the deep edge for the sauger on a jigging spoon once the current drops back. No NWS product covers Mason County at 5:50 a.m.

The window high was 26.23 at 2:15 p.m. Monday. The Summersville release is read off USGS 03189600's stage trace and 03192000's discharge trace, not from the Corps.

Its 26.12 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 6 a.m. Sunday reading (this morning's pull opens at 26.12), not 24 hours ago, and against it the rise looks like 2.48. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, up and pushing, expect colour and current, fish the slack behind anything solid. The Point Pleasant pool above is down 0.47 on the day off its own 2:15 p.m. Monday high, the Gauley above Belva read 3,980 cfs at 5 a.m. off a 5,000-cfs peak early Monday, and 03189600 below Summersville Dam dropped from 11.02 to 9.44 feet of stage between 2:45 and 4:30 a.m., a reading of the USGS traces and not a Corps statement, so the water that lifted this gauge has crested upstream and the dam is cutting back; the current below Byrd eases through the day but the color stays. At 28.6 with color and the push coming off, the fetcher's own line is still the lure problem: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon swum through the eddy below each wing dam where the pushed water slacks, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head held in the seam behind the riprap points in low light, a black-and-blue jig for the smallmouth and the drum in the slack pockets of the rock where the fish tuck out of the push, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the slack of the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark, three nights past the new moon and still near the darkest of the month; the lock wall fishes from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids when the gates open. No NWS product covers Cabell or Wayne County at 5:50 a.m.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 4:35 AM at 0.6 ft, high 10:42 AM at 4.3 ft, low 5:17 PM at 0.9 ft, high 10:58 PM at 3.4 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 3:08 AM at 0.4 ft, high 9:41 AM at 5.4 ft, low 4:07 PM at 0.6 ft, high 9:59 PM at 4.0 ft. Water 74.5F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:36 a.m. Moon waxing crescent, 5% lit, 2.0 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 10:42 AM and 10:58 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Third day past the new moon: the fetcher's file carries the moon as a waxing crescent, 5 percent lit and 2.0 days old, Saturday's new moon as Monday's U.S. Naval Observatory check placed it, with the first quarter Oct. 18 and the full moon Oct. 26, so the spring tides are still on, big swings and hard inlet current, though the surf swing has come down from 5.3 feet Monday to 5.0 today. NWS Wilmington had no product for Coastal Pender at 5:50 a.m., no rip current statement, no high surf advisory, no coastal flood advisory, the second quiet beach morning in a row. The sound at Hampstead came off a 0.6-foot low at 4:35 a.m. and fills 3.7 feet to a 4.3-foot high at 10:42 a.m.; it then drains 3.4 feet to a 0.9-foot low at 5:17 p.m., so the last two hours of the ebb, about 3:15 to 5:17 p.m., land in the late afternoon, and fills 2.5 feet to a 3.4-foot high at 10:58 p.m., after dark; all four sound events fall inside Tuesday. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 3:08 a.m. at 0.4, high 9:41 a.m. at 5.4, low 4:07 p.m. at 0.6, high 9:59 p.m. at 4.0, a 5.0- and 4.8-foot swing against Monday's 5.3 and 5.2. Today's lags from the two tables are 61 and 59 minutes on the highs and 87 and 70 minutes on the lows, against 56 and 54 and 84 and 72 on Monday; the lows again lag longer than the highs, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat hour's offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 74.5 degrees at 5:36 a.m., up 1.1 from Monday's 73.4 and back above Saturday's 74.3. What is running is 12 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:51 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings starting to show at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, and inshore red drum as the main target, scattered through the ICW, the creeks and the inlets, with no trout reports yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, a few trout on early topwater, glass minnows thick off the beach and the kings still in 50 to 60 feet; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout in the first hour of light on Spook Jrs. and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds on shrimp at the bridges and oyster reefs; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or Gulp under popping corks, flounder as bycatch, false albacore due on the nearshore structure; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small metal and epoxy jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under diving birds and kings in the 8- to 12-mile range. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait everywhere, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem: the 10:42 a.m. high puts spring-tide water over the grass and up the dock pilings, which is where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 8:45 to 10:42 a.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the ebb, roughly 3:15 to 5:17 p.m., a daylight spring ebb with no beach product over it: finger mullet and shrimp are the forage and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead; on the evening flood, 5:17 to 10:58 p.m., a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they cover, and the dock lights are the trout spot once the near-moonless dark sets in toward the 10:58 p.m. high, though with the water at Beaufort back up to 74.5 the cool-down the report says the trout are waiting on has not held. The surf side, with no advisory on it and 5.4 feet of water at the pier on the 9:41 a.m. high, is Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs for the Spanish and bluefish on the morning flood and cut bait on the bottom for the slot reds in the evening, the pattern every pier in the report gives. Slack at 10:42 a.m., 5:17 p.m. and 10:58 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only.
